# Extents

> Escrow for real-world outcomes on NEAR. A sponsor funds an objective in USDC on the NEAR Intents Verifier; it pays the contributors only if an evaluator attests that the objective was achieved against a published spec, and returns everything to the sponsor otherwise. Testnet only, against Tidepool's Verifier (`verifier.tidepool-sandbox.testnet`).

Agents can draft and launch objectives for a sponsor, read their state, check specs, take a contributor's part, and evaluate deliveries for an evaluator. Agents never sign: every transaction belongs to a wallet or a Sputnik DAO. Whatever a person can do in a browser, they do on the objective's page: give them its link rather than raw transactions when they have no signer of their own.

## Use it

- [Agent skill](/skill.md): the recipes, step by step: draft, deploy and hand an objective to its sponsor; contribute to one; cancel or release one for its sponsor; evaluate one for its evaluator; sign with a NEAR Intents Agent API account.
- `https://<this host>/o/{objective}`: the objective's page, for people. Its terms and live state; contributors commit, check and deliver there, and the evaluator checks and attests there, each in their own wallet. Every API answer about an objective carries this link as `page`.

## API

Plain JSON over HTTPS. Send `content-type: application/json`. Errors are `{"error": "…"}` with status 400 (bad input; the message says what), 404, 429 (the hourly allowance is spent; retry later) or 502 (a chain read or the deploy failed; retry). Amounts are decimal strings. Nothing is ever signed or sent for you, except `POST /api/deploy`, which anyone may call.

- `POST /api/tools/propose_spec` — body: a spec (`{v: 1, statement, criteria: [{id, description, check: {kind, …}}], max_report_bytes?}`). Returns `{ok: true, spec_hash}` or `{ok: false, error}`: fix the error and check again.
- `POST /api/tools/check_accounts` — body `{accounts: ["a.testnet", …]}` (1 to 12). Returns each account mapped to whether it exists.
- `POST /api/tools/verifier_balance` — body `{account}`. Returns `{USDC: "12.5"}`: what the account holds on the Verifier.
- `POST /api/tools/view_objective` — body `{objective}`. The same as `GET /api/objective/{objective}`.
- `GET /api/objective/{objective}` — `{deployed, state?: {funded, committed, delivered, taken, deadline, outcome?, owed, in_flight}, documents?: {params, spec}, verifier_balance, evaluator_dao?}`. `committed`, `delivered` and `taken` are bitmasks over the contributors in `params` order; `funded` is in base units (6 decimals); `documents` are present only once published and checked against the address; `evaluator_dao` (`{proposal_bond, proposers}`) when the evaluator is a Sputnik DAO.
- `POST /api/draft` — body `{proposal: {spec, contributors: {account: percent}, evaluator, deadline, amount, acceptance_window_hours?}, sponsor, salt?}`. Percents sum to 100 (at most 10 contributors); `deadline` is RFC 3339 UTC; `amount` is in USDC. Returns `{objective, page, params, spec, transactions: [publish, fund], fund_intent}`; each transaction is `{step, signer, receiver, method, args, gas, deposit?, near_call, note?}`, where `near_call` is the same call as a raw NEAR function call, `{receiver_id, method_name, args, gas, deposit?}` with gas in gas units and deposit in yoctoNEAR as decimal strings. `page` is the launch link: the terms ride in its fragment, and the sponsor who opens it deploys, publishes and funds in their browser wallet; the page refuses terms that don't derive its address. `fund_intent` is the same funding as a Verifier `transfer` intent (`{intent, receiver_id, tokens, msg}`), for a sponsor that signs intents rather than NEAR transactions: sign it with `signer_id` = the sponsor and relay it with `execute_intents`. Keep `params.salt`: drafting again with it gives the same objective.
- `POST /api/deploy` — body `{params, spec?}` (exactly as `/api/draft` returned them). Deploys the objective's contract at its derived address. With `spec`, this app's deployer also publishes the terms, so a sponsor with no NEAR key need not; the spec must match `params.spec_hash`. Idempotent, and it cannot change the terms. Returns `{accountId, txHash?, published?}`: `published` is false when the terms were already readable.
- `POST /api/objective/{objective}/contribute` — body `{account, report?, delivery_tx?, delivery_signer?}`. A contributor's part, one step at a time; nothing is sent. Returns `{objective, page, account, slot, committed, delivered, report_sha256?, next, transactions}`: `next` says in words what to do, and `transactions` holds the call to sign now. Not committed: `[commit]`. Committed, with `report` (the exact text, at most 200,000 characters and the spec's `max_report_bytes`): `[deliver]`, carrying its SHA-256. Committed and not yet delivered, a `withdraw` is added: it gives the slot back, open again to the contributor or, after `commit_by`, to its backup. Delivered, with `report` and `delivery_tx` (the finalized `ob_deliver` transaction; `delivery_signer` only when a relayer signed it): `[publish]`. Once the objective is resolved or past its last moment to attest, a `close` anyone may sign is added. 400 when the account holds no slot or the report is longer than the terms allow.
- `POST /api/objective/{objective}/sponsor` — empty body. The sponsor's part after launch; nothing is sent. Returns `{objective, page, sponsor, funded, next, transactions, cancel_intent?, release_intent?}`: `next` says in words what to do, and `transactions` holds the call `sponsor` may sign now. `cancel_intent` and `release_intent` are the same `cancel` and `release` as Verifier `auth_call` intents (`{intent, contract_id, msg, min_gas}`), for a sponsor that signs intents rather than NEAR transactions: sign one with `signer_id` = the sponsor and relay it with `execute_intents`; each is present with its transaction, when `params.auth_caller` names the Verifier, as it does in every objective `/api/draft` builds. While no slot is committed: `[cancel]` (`ob_cancel`: everything funded returns, and the objective resolves as `cancelled`). While a slot is committed and not every slot has delivered: `[]`, and `next` names who is awaited. Once every slot delivered, until the last moment to attest: `[release]` (the sponsor's own `ob_attest` achieved, with no review hash: it pays the contributors by their shares, and the objective resolves as `released`); none when the sponsor is the evaluator, whose attestation is the verdict (use `/review`), or when this deployment's contract build has no release. Once the objective is resolved or past its last moment to attest, a `close` anyone may sign. 400 when the objective has no published terms.
- `POST /api/objective/{objective}/review` — empty body. Checks every criterion against the reports delivered on chain, as the evaluator would. Returns `{summary, results: [{criterion_id, outcome: pass|fail|skipped, detail}], delivered, missing?, review?, params, evaluator_dao?, page, transactions?}`. With `review`, `transactions` are `[publish, attest]`, or `[publish, propose]` for a DAO evaluator. Without it, a check could not run (see each result's `detail`): try again later, and never attest without a review.
- `POST /api/check` and `POST /api/evaluate` — the same checks streamed live as AG-UI 1.0 over SSE, for pages. `forwardedProps = {objective, deliverable: {text}}` or `{objective}`; each criterion is a `check` tool call, its result a `TOOL_CALL_RESULT`, and `RUN_FINISHED.result` the summary.
- `POST /api/agent` — the customer agent this app runs, AG-UI 1.0 over SSE. Send `forwardedProps.account` (the sponsor) and advertise the frontend tool `launch_objective`; the run ends with it pending in `RUN_FINISHED.outcome.pendingToolCallIds`, and its draft streams as `STATE_SNAPSHOT`s.

## Protocol

- Each objective is its own contract at a NEP-616 deterministic address (`0s…`) derived from its `Params`, so the address commits to the terms.
<!-- Restates docs/spec.md, "A holder may withdraw until it delivers"; docs/spec.md, "The sponsor may cancel until someone commits"; docs/spec.md, "The sponsor may release but never fail"; docs/spec.md, "Only the Verifier relays signed calls"; docs/spec.md, "Publishing to an objective changes nothing"; docs/spec.md, "Only the sponsor funds"; docs/spec.md, "A verdict follows its results"; docs/spec.md, "A judged spec caps the report size" -->
- The rules the contract enforces: https://github.com/MultiAgency/extents/blob/main/docs/spec.md#7-rules
- Methods: `ob_view`, `ob_commit(params)`, `ob_withdraw(params)` (the slot's holder, before delivering), `ob_deliver(params, delivery {hash})`, `ob_attest(params, attestation {verdict, review_hash?})`, `ob_cancel(params)` (the sponsor, while no slot is committed: refunds everything), `ob_close(params)`, `__fastdata_kv` (accepts document publication as a no-op), and funding through the Verifier's `mt_transfer_call` with `msg = {"params": …, "action": {"action": "fund"}}`. Only the sponsor's funding is accepted.
- Events (`EVENT_JSON`, standard `extents-objective`): `funded`, `committed`, `delivered`, `resolved`, `paid`, `lost`, `cleanup`.
- The spec (`spec_hash` in `Params`) and the review (`review_hash` in the attestation) are JSON documents hashed as SHA-256 of their RFC 8785 canonical form. Criterion kinds: `contains`, `schema`, `numeric_match`, `files`, `live_url`, `sources`, `media`, `llm_judge`.
- Documents are published with FastData under the objective's own account (`__fastdata_kv`), readable from FastNEAR's KV API, under namespaced keys: `extents/v1/params` and `extents/v1/spec` by the sponsor (or, for a sponsor with no NEAR key, this app's deployer: the spec is accepted from either, pinned by `params.spec_hash`), `extents/v1/deliverable` (`{text, delivery_tx, delivery_signer}`, verified against a finalized successful delivery event) by each contributor, `extents/v1/review` by the evaluator. A reader trusts a row only when it matches an on-chain commitment or its writer holds the role.
- A review's verdict follows its results: `achieved` needs every criterion to pass and no slot `missing`; `failed` needs a criterion to fail or a slot to be `missing` (a slot with no verified report). A spec with an `llm_judge` sets `max_report_bytes`, the UTF-8 bytes allowed per report; a longer report fails the judged criteria without any model being asked, so that `fail` carries no `llm_calls` (a judged `pass` always needs every model's call). A contributor's cited host that stays unreachable for 10 minutes across two evaluations fails its criterion. On chain, `achieved` is refused unless every slot delivered. A fetching check that passes carries the SHA-256 of what it fetched. An `llm_judge` names one model or three; each answers once on NEAR AI Cloud with the request `crates/spec` defines, the majority decides, and each call's `llm_calls` entry (criterion, model, answer, hashes) carries NEAR AI's ed25519 signature over `<model>:<sha256(request)>:<sha256(response)>`.

The app does not support launching file-delivery criteria. Network/model uncertainty is skipped, not a failed verdict.
An unknown funding outcome must be reconciled, never replaced on a timer. The effective attestation deadline is state.deadline.
Unattributed balances are retained. Receipt keys come from provider HTTPS unless pinned; TEE attestation is not verified.
